# paperclip_company (Resource)

Manages a Paperclip company, the top-level container for agents, goals and projects.

~> Destroying this resource permanently deletes the company together with everything in it, including agents, tasks and history that were not created by Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "paperclip_company" "studio" {
  name        = "Greenlight Studio"
  description = "Develops, produces and releases short films."

  # A monthly spending limit of 500.00 for the whole company.
  budget_monthly_cents = 50000

  # Required for paperclip_agent, which creates agents without a hire approval.
  require_board_approval_for_new_agents = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the company.

### Optional

- `budget_monthly_cents` (Number) Monthly spending limit for the whole company, in cents. `0` (the default) means no limit.
- `description` (String) What the company does. Agents see this as their mission.
- `require_board_approval_for_new_agents` (Boolean) Whether new agents need board approval before they exist. `paperclip_agent` creates agents directly, which the API only allows when this is `false`. Defaults to the value chosen by the Paperclip instance.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the company.
- `issue_prefix` (String) Prefix used for the identifiers of the company's tasks.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status of the company: `active`, `paused` or `archived`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Companies are imported by their identifier.
terraform import paperclip_company.studio 3f0e4a52-6c1b-4f0e-9a43-0d1e6f5a7b21
```
